subject: Post-call: Medifica inference deep-dive — SLOs, topology options & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@medifica.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@medifica.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Medifica inference deep-dive — SLOs, topology options & next steps

Hi Samantha / Ravi —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and visible next steps. I wrote this up while the discussion was fresh; flag anything I missed.

Pain points / goals you shared
- Real-time triage assistant for clinical intake: P95 latency target ~120 ms at typical request size (avg 350 tokens).
- Peak throughput during business hours: ~20 req/s initial, plan to scale to 100 req/s in Q2.
- Strong data governance: PHI-in-scope, requirement for VPC/private deployment and audit logs.
- Cost sensitivity: need predictable per-req economics for budgeting.

Technical constraints we captured
- Primary model family: 16B decoder-only variants; open to 8B if throughput gains + quality hold.
- Typical sequence lengths: 250–450 tokens for prompts, KV reuse expected across multi-step clinical flows.
- Preferred cloud region: us-west-2 (near Medifica infra).

Options we discussed
1) Redwood Private (VPC): customer-managed VPC with private control plane; meets PHI/KMS requirements.
2) Dedicated (reserved): Redwood-managed GPU pool pinned to your account for predictable throughput and SLAs.
3) Hosted API (short term): possible for non-PHI or dev testing but not acceptable for production PHI.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Karthik: provide throughput/latency projection matrix for 8B vs 16B models with batching and recommended KV cache config — by Thu, Dec 16.
- Marissa: draft reserved-capacity pricing options and a short comparison of Dedicated vs Private (cost + ops tradeoffs) — by Mon, Dec 20.
- Irene: prepare a one-page SOW template and HubSpot playbook link; schedule a follow-up technical review for engineers — propose Wed, Dec 22.

Attachments I’ll share after this note: sample SLO CSV we discussed, initial SOW draft, and a short PDF summarizing Dedicated vs Private.

Thanks — great conversation and clear set of priorities.

Irene Choi
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for the concise summary. This matches our notes. Couple clarifications from our end:

- The 120 ms P95 is strict for the triage endpoint only. Downstream summarization can be relaxed to 500 ms P95.
- For throughput estimates, the 100 req/s is an FY28-Q1 stretch goal; please include a 50 req/s mid range for capacity planning.
- PHI: we require customer-managed KMS and full audit log retention for 2 years.

We’d like the technical review to include our platform engineers. Ravi and the platform team (platform@medifica.com) are copied — they’ll take Karthik’s projection and validate our limits.

Thanks —
Samantha

Subject: Re: Post-call: Medifica inference deep-dive — SLOs, topology options & next steps

Thanks — looping in technical detail below (high-level), plus what I’ll attach for your engineers. I’ll produce the projection matrix by Thu.

Quick notes / assumptions
- Model variants: baseline 16B FP16; option A = 16B int8 quantized (quality check required), option B = 8B FP16 (likely 2–3x throughput improvement).
- Hardware baseline for projections: A100 80GB (single model shard), alternative for Dedicated: 2x H100 for headroom.
- Typical prompt/response average token count used for estimates: prompt 300 tokens, generation 120 tokens.

Latency/throughput guidance (back-of-envelope)
- 16B FP16 (A100 80GB): single-request cold-start ~350–450 ms; steady-state (with KV cache + batching) P95 ~140–180 ms at 20 req/s; with optimized batching profile and prefix caching we can approach ~120 ms P95 at 20 req/s.
- 8B FP16: P95 can be ~60–90 ms under the same conditions.
- Int8 quantization on 16B: potential ~25–40% throughput gain but needs evaluation on your prompt set for hallucination/quality risk.

Operational notes
- KV caching: given multi-step flows, enabling prefix/KV reuse across session windows will reduce compute by ~30% for your workload shape.
- Fallback policy: recommend routing triage endpoint to Dedicated (pinned) and summarization to Hosted variants with automatic fallback to smaller model if queue depth or GPU saturation occurs.
- PHI & compliance: Private (VPC) + customer KMS meets the strictest requirement; Dedicated in a private tenancy may also meet needs but requires an attestation for key management.

Attachments I’ll send now:
- redwood_dedicated_vpc_options.pdf (deployment matrix)
- medifica_slo_samples.csv (the same sample referenced by Irene — with example token distributions)

- Redwood: run 8B pilot and provide a P95 matrix (8B vs 16B, int8 trial) and a short quality regression note — deliver by Fri Dec 17.
- Commercial: Marissa will follow up with two pricing constructs (Dedicated reserve vs Private deployment) and a draft SOW for review.

Proposed follow-up call: Wed Dec 22, 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite after Marissa posts the pricing note.

Closing note: we’ll include a short runbook in the SOW that captures automatic fallback routing and KPIs we’ll monitor during pilot (P95 latency, error-rate, cost per 1k tokens).
